evidence: Acceptance criterion 1 requires the request builder to use https://graph.microsoft.com/.default.
auth.py exposes a caller-controlled scope argument and directly serializes it into the OAuth request, so callers can construct a narrower or unrelated scope.
The request-shape test exercises only the default and does not prove that overriding the required scope is impossible.
findings.remediation: Remove the public scope parameter from build_client_credentials_request and always serialize APP_ONLY_SCOPE. Add a regression test showing the builder has no supported path that substitutes another scope.
findings.title: Client-credentials request builder does not enforce the required .default scope
findings.verification: Run the focused auth tests and inspect the builder signature/body to confirm every generated client-credentials request contains exactly https://graph.microsoft.com/.default.

evidence: Acceptance criterion 6 explicitly requires race tests for logout or a new start()/start_app_only() while an initial or renewal request is outstanding.
The candidate tests initial acquisition against logout and start_app_only, and renewal against logout and start_app_only.

There is no corresponding initial-acquisition or renewal race test where device-code start() supersedes the in-flight app-only operation. The implementation's shared generation counter appears intended to handle this, but the mandated evidence is absent.
findings.remediation: Add deterministic callback-race tests in which start() runs during both an initial start_app_only request and an app-only renewal. Assert the stale response cannot install a token or restore app-only secret state and that the newer device-code session remains authoritative.
findings.title: Required device-code supersession race cases are not tested
findings.verification: Run tests.test_auth and confirm both new start()-during-initial-request and start()-during-renewal cases pass.

limitations: The sandbox prevented independent completion of all three mandatory commands: loopback binding is prohibited, bytecode output cannot be written, and no writable temporary directory is available.
The committed handoff reports 112 tests passing plus clean compile and governance validation outside this review sandbox, but author-recorded results are not independent command evidence.
No live Microsoft tenant authentication was performed; the approved issue explicitly excludes that protected action.
Because mandatory execution evidence is incomplete, repository rules require BLOCKED regardless of the independently passing focused authentication tests or the substantive findings.
review.summary: Review blocked by the sandbox's inability to complete the mandatory full test, compile, and governance checks. Independent focused authentication tests pass, but two required changes were identified: the request builder permits callers to override the mandated .default scope, and the acceptance-required device-code start() supersession race cases are missing from the tests.
